rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rīsh denotes both birds’ wings and decorated clothing.
rows.anchor: is used for the wings of birds and it also refers to decorated clothes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing primarily covers the body, while embellishment is also a proper purpose God provided for human nature.
rows.anchor: The foremost purpose of clothes is to cover the body. However, embellishment is also included in its purposes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither covering nor adornment is wrong in itself; disorder comes from either extreme, and the Qur’an rejects ascetic contempt for clothes and sacred nudity.
rows.anchor: None of these objectives in itself is wrong. However, just as going to both extremes creates disorder in everything

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inner piety is a superior garment that makes the genuine benefits of outward clothing possible.
rows.anchor: Besides an outward attire, human beings are also blessed with an inner one and that is the attire of piety.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without piety, a clothed person is inwardly naked, and clothing may magnify arrogance or ugliness instead of dignity.
rows.anchor: If this does not exist, then a person is naked in spite of wearing clothes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Piety grows from modesty, fear of God, and servitude, giving its bearer an angelic grace.
rows.anchor: This attire of piety emanates from modesty, fear of God and a sense of servitude to Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder recalls the primordial directions given to Adam’s progeny when they entered earthly life.
rows.anchor: the progeny of Adam (sws) were directed when he was sent in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh are warned that Satan has subjected them to the same trial that confronted Adam.
rows.anchor: The purpose is warn the Quraysh that they have been inflicted with the same trial

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi identifies the guidance in 7:35 with the same guidance given to Adam’s progeny, protecting them from Adam-like trials; he cites 2:38 as its parallel.
rows.anchor: In my opinion, here too the same guidance is being referred which was given to the progeny of Adam (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing humanity as Adam’s children invokes a shared family story and makes a father’s experience a powerful lesson for descendants.
rows.anchor: The incidents and events that occur in the life of a father are the strongest means of learning a lesson for the children.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Descendants preserve and pass down loyalty to a father’s friends and enmity toward his foes; Arabs maintain this inherited tradition even without judging its merits.
rows.anchor: They preserve this etched in their minds and transmit it to later generations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity should remember Satan’s declared, jealousy-driven enmity toward Adam and all his descendants through Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: So it is a matter of great sorrow if human beings forget the enmity of Satan and his progeny

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many descendants go beyond forgetting and befriend Satan and his allies, letting them lead them toward the ruin intended for Adam.
rows.anchor: many among them have actually befriended this enemy and his associates.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is so eloquent that sincere descendants feel anger toward Satan, while only the dishonorable remain unmoved.
rows.anchor: When every honourable and sincere son of Adam (sws) reads these words of address and the reminders they sound, his blood boils against Satan.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s social strategy begins by stripping away inward piety, the honor God gives alongside outward clothing.
rows.anchor: he first strips people off the attire of piety which the Almighty has revealed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once modesty is lost, clothing feels burdensome and fashion can make people appear naked while dressed.
rows.anchor: After that fashion comes to their rescue and human beings wear such clothes that even after wearing them, they appear naked.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Society can come to call nudity culture and clothing obsolete, as learned devils recast nudity as nature and dress as imposed custom.
rows.anchor: Then gradually people become bereft of intellect to such an extent that nudity becomes the name of culture

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This process fills society with lust and lewdness until it merits destruction and replacement.
rows.anchor: the whole society is impregnated with the poison of lust and lewdness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s many disguises and attack locations make his agents hard to recognize or guard against; his army includes jinn and humans.
rows.anchor: The army of Satan boasts both of jinn and mankind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s agents hide as apparent friends, teachers, or leaders while seeking to sever people’s faith and destroy them under the guise of progress.
rows.anchor: They will regard them to be friends, well-wishers, teachers, leaders and the like

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exploit people’s inner weaknesses with evil suggestions and charm, so humanity must stay alert to Satan’s enmity.
rows.anchor: They will know all the inner weaknesses of human beings and will try to inveigle them through evil suggestions.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adherence to faith in God and His revealed guidance protects people from Satan’s assaults, as the promise in 2:38 indicates.
rows.anchor: they must strongly adhere to faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who deprive themselves of faith become Satan’s target; their empty hearts are inhabited by devils.
rows.anchor: only people who deprive themselves of faith become a target of Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose hearts are full of faith in God and His guidance remain protected from Satan and his accomplices.
rows.anchor: people whose hearts are replete with faith in God and in His guidance remain secure from Satan and his accomplices.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan deceived the Quraysh as he deceived Adam and Eve, prompting naked circumambulation at the Ka‘bah as he had prompted their undressing in the Garden.
rows.anchor: he has succeeded in making the Quraysh take off their clothes in the House of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh mistake this satanic trial for ancestral custom and God’s command, though Satan intends to expel them from the House as he expelled Adam and Eve from Paradise.
rows.anchor: The irony is that they think that this is a tradition of their forefathers and a directive of God.

rows.speaker: exegetes
rows.claim: Exegetes identify fāḥishah as naked circumambulation; Islahi accepts this view as likely because the Quraysh treated the act as divinely directed.
rows.anchor: Our exegetes think that it refers to the tradition

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the Quraysh considered themselves exempt from the nakedness rule, they imposed it on other Arabs.
rows.anchor: Though the Quraysh themselves considered themselves to be above this directive, they regarded it to be applicable to others.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Non-Quraysh Arabs had to borrow Qurayshi clothes or circumambulate naked, since outsiders’ clothes were treated as worldly adornment unfit for worship.
rows.anchor: Either they should borrow it from the Quraysh or circumabulate the House of God while being naked.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi compares this contempt for clothing with ascetic customs in temples and churches, which priests and worshippers invented and sacralized.
rows.anchor: All of them were fabricated by the diabolic intentions of their priests and worshippers but were conferred with the sanctity of religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The innovation corrupted even the sacred rite of circumambulation and became embedded in vulgar poetry.
rows.anchor: This became so deeply rooted in their culture that such vices became part of their vulgar poetry.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan entered the House under a guise of sanctity and converted worship of God into worship of himself, illustrating the warning in 7:27.
rows.anchor: Satan infiltrated in the House of God in the garb of sanctity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s attributes and human nature both reject the claim that He would command public nakedness, especially at His own House.
rows.anchor: How can God order him to be naked and that too in the vicinity of His own House?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisṭ, or fairness, is the comprehensive balance underlying the sharī‘ah and all religious directives.
rows.anchor: Qisṭ is an all-embracing reality which is also the essence of the sharī‘ah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fairness applies across beliefs, deeds, morals, worship, economics, politics, and society.
rows.anchor: It is inclusive of beliefs, deeds, morality, worship as well as directives related to economics, politics and society.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God is master, fairness requires worship of Him alone; since He created and sustains people, fairness also requires accountability and recompense.
rows.anchor: when God is the master, then it is against fairness to worship someone other than Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God did not hold people accountable and reward or punish them, that would be injustice rather than fairness.
rows.anchor: then He should hold them accountable and reward or punish them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fairness rules out abandoning clothes, food, or drink for worship; people should enjoy them in moderation.
rows.anchor: it is against fairness that clothes be forsaken for God’s worship or eating and drinking be abandoned.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mosque and prostration belong to God alone, so worshippers should not face or invoke anyone else; Islahi cites 72:18.
rows.anchor: Prostration is due before God only and hence a mosque by its very nature is specific for God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel wording about sincerity shows that obedience, like worship, is owed exclusively to God.
rows.anchor: They show that it is not just God’s worship that entails sincerity, His obedience also entails sincerity; none else can be included in it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should worship and obey their Creator alone because they return to Him alone, without alleged deities or intercessors.
rows.anchor: just as they came into this world alone, they will go back to Him alone; none of their alleged deities and intercessors will be with them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise return-to-God statement links the afterlife with monotheism and points to an evident proof of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: a very evident proof of the hereafter is also pointed to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires one faction toward the truth, while another strays by befriending devils and will meet the fate they threatened.
rows.anchor: one faction was led astray; it has befriended the devils

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing people as Adam’s children reminds Quraysh and the Arabs that Satan is humanity’s eternal enemy and following him means befriending their father’s foe.
rows.anchor: It gives this message to every human being that Satan is their eternal enemy.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zīnah here means ordinary clothing, not embellished clothing; the naked-tawaf custom rested on treating clothes as adornment unfit for worship.
rows.anchor: The word زﻳﻨﺖ( zīnah) does not mean adorned clothes. It refers to mere clothes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs’ stripping of men and women from iḥrām was a jāhili innovation; the command to wear clothes at every mosque reforms it and refutes monastic nudity.
rows.anchor: By using the expression “every mosque” the directive was generalized and was not made specific to the House of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both severe deprivation and excess violate fairness; God calls for moderation in clothing, eating, and drinking.
rows.anchor: This imbalance refers to both extremes: doing something very little or crossing the limits in doing it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neither indulgence that makes food and clothing life’s purpose nor ascetic renunciation is desired; moderation is required throughout life.
rows.anchor: Neither does He like that a person make eating, drinking and clothing a purpose of his life and spend all his time in these

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard of moderation is left to human nature and reason, varies by circumstance and person, and requires the wealthy to recognize others’ rights in their wealth.
rows.anchor: It can vary with respect to circumstances and from person to person.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealthy may benefit from their resources but must avoid overspending or wrongful uses; God’s rejection of such people signifies anger.
rows.anchor: he can benefit from it but not overspend or spend on wrong things

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about who forbade God’s adornment and wholesome food is rhetorical: only God can prohibit what He gives.
rows.anchor: none except God has the authority to do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s creation of these goods for His servants is evidence that they are meant for human use; restrictions require proof from their giver.
rows.anchor: these things by their very existence bear witness that they have been made by God for people

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed parallel words mean worldly favors are primarily believers’ right though disbelievers receive a share, while the next life’s favors belong exclusively to believers, who remain accountable for worldly use.
rows.anchor: these favours will be entirely for the believers and the disbelievers will have no share in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enjoying worldly blessings is compatible with piety when people avoid excess and continue to fulfill God’s and other people’s rights.
rows.anchor: The correct attitude in this regard is to benefit from them but not over indulge in them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance that God explains His revelations comforts believers, and the verb explain signals intention.
rows.anchor: the verb “explain” signifies intention.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage exposes the Quraysh for calling lawful what God prohibits and treating as unlawful what He permits under a religious guise.
rows.anchor: the Quraysh have regarded as lawful and in fact part of religion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibited fawāḥish include both public and hidden lewd acts, which Islahi says were explained at 6:151.
rows.anchor: lewd acts), whether they are apparent or hidden.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rebelliousness against God is inherently wrongful; calling it wrongful emphasizes its heinousness, since no one may arrogantly cross His bounds.
rows.anchor: It means to rebel against the directives of God. It is qualified by the adjective “wrongful.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in God accords with reason and nature, but associating partners requires conclusive evidence because it undermines reason, nature, justice, and fairness.
rows.anchor: An idolater also believes in God. As for ascribing partners to God is concerned, it needs proof and that too of a conclusive nature.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fabricating religious permissions or prohibitions from personal whims and attributing them to God is forbidden; this entails the need for messengers who convey proof.
rows.anchor: These words also express the need for prophets and messengers

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūrah primarily warns Quraysh, and the preceding accusations form a charge sheet that leaves them no excuse before the discourse returns to its main subject.
rows.anchor: What is stated above is merely a charge sheet meant to leave them with no excuse.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nation’s fixed term warns Quraysh that delayed punishment is not acquittal; God’s established destruction of rebellious peoples will come when their appointed time arrives, without delay or advance.
rows.anchor: they should not think that they would never be called to account.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An individual’s term is measured in time units, while a nation’s term depends on the decline of its faith and morals until it reaches a limit warranting destruction.
rows.anchor: Their time is determined on the basis of decadence of their faith and morals.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone knows when an individual or nation reaches its end and when continued existence conflicts with divine wisdom.
rows.anchor: the time of death of nations too is in His knowledge only.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending a messenger completes the communication of truth to a nation; if it then denies the messenger, God destroys it, a rule discussed further in Sūrah Yūnus.
rows.anchor: when a messenger is sent to a nation, it signifies conclusive communication of the truth to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls God’s promise to Adam and his descendants to send messengers as protection from Satan; Quraysh must follow the messenger reciting God’s revelations, as 2:38 states.
rows.anchor: This promise of sending His messengers was made by the Almighty with Adam (sws) and his progeny

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human intellect and nature themselves attest to the need for divine guidance.
rows.anchor: human intellect and nature vouch for the need of this divine guidance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise was fulfilled through a series of prophets, including pious descendants who answered the angels’ negative expectation about Adam’s progeny.
rows.anchor: the Almighty negated the notion of the angels about the progeny of Adam (sws) through pious individuals born to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿan with istikbār conveys evasion; those who deny and evade the messengers’ revelations will dwell in Hell.
rows.anchor: which encompasses the meaning of evasion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding reminders, the discourse directly addresses Quraysh from verse 37 onward.
rows.anchor: Now from verse 37, the Quraysh are directly addressed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who invent lies about God or deny His revelations are gravely unjust; at death their alleged deities are absent and they confess their disbelief.
rows.anchor: they will bear witness against themselves that undoubtedly they remained in disbelief.
